problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}$ and ${R}^{3},$ respectively. 

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$
- ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$
- ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{1}+{c}_{3}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{3}$

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}$ is a linearly independent set in ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
- $[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}$
- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. Notice that

$$
1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

where some coefficients are nonzero, so the set is linearly dependent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]=1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+5\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

- Statement III is false. Since the set is not linearly independent, it can't form a basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
